notes: Deleting a message now means it can be un-learned. Until this build, removing a message only cleared it from the recent history the characters are shown word for word — anything already written down from it stayed in their memory and kept going out with every reply, which is why steering a conversation by deleting worked for a few messages and then quietly drifted back. Each memory now records which stretch of conversation it was read out of. Delete a message that taught a character something and it offers to forget it, showing you exactly what it found first; rewind to a point and it offers everything learned from there onwards; clear a conversation and it offers the lot. It offers rather than does, because a memory can be worth keeping even when the message that produced it was a misfire, and nothing is forgotten without being read first. In a group it names which character remembers what, since each of them keeps their own version. Memories from before this build carry no record of where they came from, so they are matched by when they were written, which is close but not exact — those are offered on a rewind, where the timing is a fair guess, and never on a clear, where it would sweep up things learned in other chats.
